vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Renovate matches an alert against the Cargo.toml requirement before Cargo.lock, so a lockfile-only fix leaves `1.43.0` still matching `< 1.43.1` and the next patch release opens another PR. `bump` raises the requirement to the fixed version, which ends the alert in one PR.

packageRules.description: config:recommended commits cargo dependencies as `fix`, which release-plz lists under Fixed. `chore` lands under Other.

cargo_metadata 0.21 and later need Rust 1.86. Renovate cannot skip cargo releases by rust-version: `constraints.rust` takes a release channel such as `1.85`, which constraintsFiltering reads as `^1.85`. Lift this cap with the MSRV.
MSRV bumps must be a deliberate human change, not a side effect of a dependency PR. resolver 3 in Cargo.toml keeps transitive crates within rust-version. The cap above covers direct ones.
Actions and runners only need bumping when GitHub deprecates them, so they get their own six-monthly group. Security fixes ignore the schedule.

customManagers.description: The nightly pin used by the Rustfmt job and cargo doc. A new nightly can reformat the tree, so the Rustfmt job may fail the PR until someone runs fmt on its branch.
Runner labels in the build matrix. The github-actions manager reads a literal `runs-on`, not `${{ matrix.os }}`.
